objConvention: JudeanFloraV1; canonical UE cm (X east, +Y south, Z up), written with Y reflected and triangle winding reversed for the legacy OBJ importer adapter. One o object, no g groups, so the importer creates exactly one material slot.

partKinds.solid: closed shell, every edge used exactly twice, canonical signed volume > 0
partKinds.card: alpha-tested leaf cards written back to back: closed shell, signed volume 0. A card emitted once leaves an open shell and fails the check.
partKinds.billboard: one open single-sided quad for a camera-facing material; exempt from both checks, and the exemption is recorded here rather than implied

adapterReadback: Every OBJ is re-read after writing. Reflecting Y back must reproduce canonicalBoundsCm, and a solid mesh's FILE-SPACE signed volume must be negative - that sign is what proves the Y-reflect plus reversed winding was applied exactly once.

partChecks.windingCheckExempt: single open camera-facing quad; a closed-shell or signed-volume test is meaningless for it

textures.note: Generated procedurally with the standard library only - no PIL, no numpy, no photograph. The atlas is 2x2 and each cell depicts a spray of leaves spanning cardSpanCm in the world, with each leaf drawn at leafLengthCm / cardSpanCm of the cell - so a 6 cm olive leaf renders at 6 cm rather than at whatever fraction of a crown-sized card it used to land on. A palm cell depicts ONE frond with its pinnae, since a palm card is one frond. The alpha edge is hard so an alpha-test threshold of 0.5 is unambiguous, and the billboard render cuts its silhouette from the same mask the atlas was written from.
textures.billboardNote: An orthographic render of this species' own LOD1 mesh, so the impostor is a picture of the tree it replaces.

species.label: olive
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Olea europaea; cultivated Judean groves run 5-10 m with a 4-8 m crown
species.mikdashSource: Olive oil for the Menorah, Shemot 27:20 and Mishnah Menachot 8:4-5, which ranks the oil of Tekoa first. The Mount of Olives itself is named in Zecharyah 14:4, and Mishnah Parah 3:6 has the causeway run from the Temple Mount to it for the Red Heifer.
species.growsThere: The characteristic cultivated tree of the terraced Judean hillsides.

species.label: Jerusalem pine
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Pinus halepensis; 10-20 m in the Judean hills, taller only on deep soil
species.growsThere: The dominant conifer of the Jerusalem hills and of a century of afforestation on them; it is what a modern eye reads as "the hills around Jerusalem".

species.label: cypress
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Cupressus sempervirens; the columnar form is 2-5 m across at 12-22 m tall
species.mikdashSource: "Berosh" supplies the boards, floor and doors of Shlomo's Temple, Melachim I 6:15 and 6:34. The identification of berosh with Cupressus is the common one but is disputed (Juniperus excelsa and Abies cilicica are the rival readings), and that dispute is recorded rather than hidden.
species.growsThere: Native to the eastern Mediterranean hills and long planted on them.

species.label: almond
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Amygdalus communis; a small tree of 3.5-8 m
species.mikdashSource: The Menorah's cups are "meshukadim", made in the form of the almond blossom, Shemot 25:33-34. Aharon's staff bore almonds, Bamidbar 17:23.
species.growsThere: Grows wild and cultivated on the terraces; the first blossom of the Judean spring.

species.label: fig
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Ficus carica; a low, wide, often multi-stemmed tree, crown wider than tall
species.mikdashSource: One of the seven species of Devarim 8:8, from which bikkurim are brought to the Mikdash; Mishnah Bikkurim 3:1 has the fig among the first fruits marked in the field and carried up to Yerushalayim.
species.growsThere: Planted at terrace edges and beside cisterns throughout the Judean hills.

species.label: pomegranate
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Punica granatum; a large shrub or small tree of 2-5 m
species.mikdashSource: Rimonim of blue, purple and scarlet on the hem of the Kohen Gadol's me'il, Shemot 28:33-34, and two hundred rimonim in rows on the capitals of Yachin and Boaz, Melachim I 7:18-20. Also one of the seven species, Devarim 8:8.
species.growsThere: A standard terrace and garden shrub of the hills.

species.label: date palm
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Phoenix dactylifera; 12-22 m with a 6-9 m crown of pinnate fronds
species.mikdashSource: Temarim are carved on every wall, post and gate of Yechezkel's Temple, Yechezkel 40:16, 40:22, 40:26, 41:18-20 - as CARVED RELIEF, not as living trees inside the precinct. The lulav of Vayikra 23:40 and Mishnah Sukkah 3:1 is the palm frond.
species.growsThere: The date palm needs groundwater and heat; it does not grow naturally on the Jerusalem hilltops. It is therefore placed ONLY on low ground - the Kidron floor and the valley bottoms below the platform datum - and never on the ridges. Putting palms on the crest would be the single most obvious botanical error available in this landscape.

species.label: carob
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Ceratonia siliqua; a dense evergreen of 6-12 m with a broad crown
species.growsThere: Warm, sunny, south-facing rocky slopes; the Ceratonio-Pistacietum association of the Judean foothills. Its aspect preference is modelled: the band prefers the downhill bearing that faces the sun in this frame. (Choni and the carob, Ta'anit 23a, is a Judean image but not a Mikdash source, and is not claimed as one.)

species.label: terebinth
species.sizeSource: Zohary, M., Plants of the Bible (Cambridge University Press, 1982), species entry Pistacia palaestina (3-8 m) and P. atlantica (10-15 m, very broad crown); the range spans both, which is why it is wide
species.growsThere: The elah of Bereishit 35:4 and Shoftim 6:11, and one of the two climax trees of the natural Judean maquis together with Quercus calliprinos. It belongs on the shaded northern faces and in the wadis. A biblical mention is not a Mikdash connection and is not counted as one here.

species.label: Judean sage
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Salvia fruticosa; a dwarf shrub of 0.5-1.0 m
species.mikdashSource: Zohary proposed that the whorled branching of a Salvia is the botanical model behind the Menorah's form. That is a PROPOSAL about the shape of a vessel, not a source that puts sage in the Mikdash, and it is recorded as a proposal.
species.growsThere: A dominant dwarf shrub of the Judean batha on shallow rocky soil.

species.label: hyssop (ezov)
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Origanum syriacum; 0.3-0.7 m
species.mikdashSource: Ezov is bound with cedar wood and crimson wool and thrown into the burning of the Red Heifer, Bamidbar 19:6 and Mishnah Parah 3:10-11 - and that burning takes place on the Mount of Olives opposite the Temple, which is exactly this hillside. The identification of ezov with Origanum syriacum is Rambam's and is the standard one; it is an identification, not a certainty.
species.growsThere: Grows out of rock crevices and terrace walls across these hills.

species.label: rockrose
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Cistus creticus; 0.5-1.2 m
species.growsThere: The first shrub back after fire or grazing on these slopes, and the pink flush on the Judean hillsides in spring.

species.label: thorny burnet
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Sarcopoterium spinosum; a hemispherical dwarf shrub 0.3-0.6 m tall
species.growsThere: Danin, A., Flora and Vegetation of Israel (in Zohary ed.), Judean hills batha and maquis communities; Sarcopoterium is THE dominant dwarf shrub of degraded Judean batha and the single most characteristic plant of an exposed, grazed, rocky Jerusalem ridge. If one plant has to carry the bare ridges, it is this one.

species.label: dry grasses
species.binomial: Hordeum spontaneum / Avena sterilis / Stipa spp.
species.sizeSource: Zohary & Feinbrun-Dothan, Flora Palaestina vols I-IV (Israel Academy of Sciences, 1966-1986), species entry Hordeum spontaneum and Avena sterilis; culms 0.3-0.8 m
species.mikdashSource: Hordeum spontaneum is the wild ancestor of the barley of the Omer, cut on the night after the first day of Pesach from a field near Yerushalayim - Mishnah Menachot 10:2-3. The stand modelled here is wild hillside grass, not a barley field, and the Omer field is not being depicted.
species.growsThere: The dry annual grass layer that covers every un-grazed Judean slope by early summer.

materials.bark: opaque, base colour + normal, two-sided off
materials.leaf: MASKED alpha test at 0.5, TWO-SIDED, subsurface tint for the back face

limitations: No visual, collision, cook or packaged acceptance is established by this script.
Species habit is a stylised procedural approximation, not a scan or a survey.
Textures are procedural: no photograph, no third-party asset, no licence question.
